findings.claim: The adapter library exposes new `anyhow::Result` APIs, violating the project rule that `anyhow` is only allowed at binary edges.
findings.evidence: Constraint R3 states "`anyhow` only at binary edges (`frf-gateway`, `frf-cli`)"; the new `IggyBroker::new` and `IggyBroker::with_replay_retention` in `crates/frf-broker-iggy/src/broker_config.rs` return `anyhow::Result<Self>` and use `anyhow::ensure!`.
findings.suggested_fix: Return a crate-specific error type such as `IggyBrokerError` from adapter constructors and convert to `anyhow` only in `frf-gateway` composition code.

findings.claim: Snapshot responses can disclose the source position of out-of-scope or unauthorized rows through the visible snapshot barrier.
findings.evidence: `snapshot_frames` derives `barrier` directly from the projection cursor before filtering rows by tenant/type/object authorization, then pushes `SnapshotComplete { barrier, checkpoint, row_count }`; `accepted_frame` also extracts that barrier into `WatchAccepted.snapshot_barrier`. The submitted acceptance evidence says denied and out-of-scope events must not expose "source position" across the application boundary, but the test projection deliberately returns a cursor from `history.last()` even when later rows are other-type/other-tenant/denied.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not expose the full projection cursor as a visible barrier when it may have advanced due to filtered rows; keep the full offset only inside the opaque checkpoint, or compute a disclosed barrier from the last authorized in-scope delivery.
